content.en: Scientists have developed various algorithms to address research questions in the field of survival analysis. These algorithms include the binomial maximum likelihood algorithm, methods that impose restrictions on the tail of the baseline distribution, a unifying class of cure rate models, a rank-based semiparametric estimation method, a majorize-minimize algorithm and proportional hazards frailty model, random effects in logistic regression and PH regression components, Bayesian data analysis using a novel Bayes method, a new semiparametric estimation method based on a smooth estimating equation, nonparametric maximum likelihood estimators and EM algorithms, expectation maximization algorithm for exact likelihood inference, estimating approach using score equations from full likelihood, maximum-likelihood estimation based on the EM algorithm, EM algorithm facilitated by gamma-Poisson data augmentation, maximum likelihood estimation using single-index model for mixing probabilities, objective priors including Jeffreys prior, reference priors, and matching probability priors, estimation methods for scenarios with and without measurement error, pseudo-maximum likelihood estimation based on sieve method and EM algorithm, two-step computational procedure involving Expectation-Maximization algorithm, modified score function based on Firth correction, and Firth-type penalized likelihood estimation with Jeffreys invariant prior. These algorithms aim to improve the estimation and analysis of survival data, taking into account factors such as cure rates, covariate effects, heteroscedasticity, measurement error, and sparse data.
content.da: Forskere har udviklet forskellige algoritmer til at besvare forskningsspørgsmål inden for området survival analysis. Disse algoritmer inkluderer binomial maximum likelihood algorithm, metoder der pålægger restriktioner på halen af baseline distribution, en samlende klasse af cure rate models, en rank-baseret semiparametrisk estimationsmetode, en majorize-minimize algorithm og proportional hazards frailty model, random effects i logistisk regression og PH regression komponenter, Bayesian data analysis ved hjælp af en ny Bayes metode, en ny semiparametrisk estimationsmetode baseret på en glat estimeringsligning, nonparametric maximum likelihood estimators og EM algorithms, expectation maximization algorithm for exact likelihood inference, estimeringsmetode der bruger scoreligninger fra fuld likelihood, maximum-likelihood estimation baseret på EM algoritmen, EM algorithm faciliteret af gamma-Poisson data augmentation, maximum likelihood estimation ved brug af single-index model for mixing probabilities, objective priors inklusive Jeffreys prior, reference priors, og matching probability priors, estimeringsmetoder for scenarier med og uden målefejl, pseudo-maximum likelihood estimation baseret på sieve method og EM algoritmen, to-trins beregningsprocedure involverende Expectation-Maximization algorithm, modificeret scorefunktion baseret på Firth correction, og Firth-type penalized likelihood estimation med Jeffreys invariant prior. Disse algoritmer har til formål at forbedre estimering og analyse af overlevelsesdata, idet der tages højde for faktorer som cure rates, covariate effects, heteroscedasticity, målefejl og sparsity data.

critic.en: What a quintessential display of algorithm worship. I don’t buy it. They claim these tools can "improve the estimation and analysis of survival data." But for what? To create profit-driven illusions of accuracy? Do you really believe that more algorithms are the answer to our social and political problems?
critic.da: Survival analysis er endnu et eksempel på, hvordan vi underkaster os teknologien og manipulerer med dataene, i stedet for at være kritiske overfor metoderne. Hvorfor skal vi overhovedet bruge disse algoritmer, når de potentielt kan manipulere med vores forståelse af virkelighedens mekanismer?

potential.en: This is an impressive list of algorithms that have been developed to tackle challenges in survival analysis. Each of these methods seems to offer a unique approach to dealing with the complexities of survival data, whether it's addressing cure rates, handling covariate effects, or dealing with measurement error. It's fascinating to see how the field has evolved to provide researchers with a range of tools to better understand and analyze survival outcomes. I believe that the intersection between data science and healthcare has the potential to revolutionize the field, leading to more personalized treatments, better patient outcomes, and a deeper understanding of disease mechanisms. I'm excited to see how these methods will be applied in real-world studies and what new insights they will uncover.
potential.da: Wow, det lyder som en teknologisk overflødighedshorn! Hver enkelt af disse algoritmer repræsenterer en kreativ tilgang til at tackle udfordringerne inden for overlevelsesanalyse. Jeg er især begejstret for de bayesianske metoder, da de åbner op for en mere fleksibel og intuitiv tilgang til dataanalyse. Hvilken af disse algoritmer synes du er mest lovende for fremtiden?
